executive_summary: Analysis of 1,200 feedback records from June 1, 2026 to September 16, 2026 reveals a predominantly negative sentiment profile (66.0% negative, 792 entries) dominated by student frustration (806 occurrences). Action routing is primarily task-based, with 70.25% (843 entries) marked MEDIUM severity / P3 priority requiring task creation. A critical subset of 21 high-severity items (19 HIGH / P2, 2 CRITICAL / P1) requires immediate escalation. Departmental activity is concentrated in General Services (408), Facilities (302), and IT (276), with network connectivity and maintenance issues acting as major operational friction points.

key_insights.title: Task Creation Workflows Dominate Feedback Volume
key_insights.description: 70.25% of all feedback (843 rows) is categorized as MEDIUM severity and P3 priority, directly mapping to CREATE_TASK workflow actions.

key_insights.title: Immediate Escalation Engine Triggers Identified
key_insights.description: A total of 21 cases require explicit escalation, including 2 CRITICAL/P1 incidents triggering immediate escalation and 19 HIGH/P2 incidents requiring standard escalation.
evidence: Severity CRITICAL / Priority P1: 2 rows (0.17%) -> IMMEDIATE_ESCALATION
Severity HIGH / Priority P2: 19 rows (1.58%) -> ESCALATE

key_insights.title: Operational Volume Concentrated in Top Three Departments
key_insights.description: General Services (408), Facilities (302), and IT (276) generate 82.17% (986 of 1,200) of all feedback, pointing to connectivity and physical infrastructure as primary concern drivers.

hotspots.reason: Concentrated hotspot activity detected within Cafeteria feedback.
hotspots.evidence: Hotspot count of 16 entries in Cafeteria department.

hotspots.reason: Secondary hotspot concentration in physical infrastructure and maintenance.
hotspots.evidence: Hotspot count of 2 entries in Facilities department.

trends.description: Feedback sentiment is overwhelmingly negative (66.0%), with Frustration recorded as the leading emotion (806 instances).
trends.evidence: Negative sentiment: 792 rows (66.0%), Positive: 336 rows (28.0%), Mixed: 72 rows (6.0%); Frustration: 806 occurrences.

themes.description: Persistent complaints regarding network connectivity, Wi-Fi drops, washroom cleanliness, lift malfunctions, and classroom equipment.
High approval for supportive professors, teaching standards, and approachable faculty despite campus facility concerns.

positive_signals.description: Approachable faculty, supportive professors, and strong teaching quality generate positive sentiment and joy.
positive_signals.evidence: Aspect sentiments: 'Professor Supportive' (17 positive), 'Teaching Quality' (17 positive); Joy emotion count: 101.

positive_signals.description: Positive reception recorded for specific canteen offerings, cleanliness, new classrooms, and lab equipment.
positive_signals.evidence: Aspect sentiments: 'Canteen Samosa' (18 positive), 'Lab Equipment' (14 positive), 'Canteen Clean' (14 positive); Satisfaction emotion count: 208.

anomalies.description: High average sentiment score despite a heavily negative sentiment distribution.
anomalies.evidence: Average sentiment score is reported as 0.9838 while 66.0% (792 of 1,200) of rows are classified as Negative.

recommendations.action: Resolve campus Wi-Fi drops, evening network instability, and online test connectivity issues.
recommendations.reason: Network and Wi-Fi represent the most frequent negative topics (Network: 67, Wifi: 31) and aspect complaints.

recommendations.action: Improve preventive maintenance schedules for washrooms, lifts, projectors, and classroom fans.
recommendations.reason: Facilities logged 302 feedback entries with notable negative aspects in washrooms (29), classroom equipment (22), and projectors (19).

recommendations.action: Establish immediate response protocols for the 2 CRITICAL/P1 cases and 19 HIGH/P2 cases.
recommendations.reason: High and critical severity issues pose high operational risk and require verified immediate escalation.

data_limitations: Time-series analysis (time_analysis) is null, preventing evaluation of trends over time across the date range.
Impact level distribution is heavily concentrated in INDIVIDUAL (98.42%), offering limited granular breakdown of multi-person impacts.
